8.explain:
v. t. 
a) To take, grasp, get hold of.
b) To receive, obtain, gain, procure,
acquire; to collect (as taxes); to buy; to absorb, draw in; to adopt; to conceive.
c) To remove, take off.
d) As an auxiliary verb preceded by imperfect or modal converbs describes the action as performed in the interest, on behalf, at the wish, or in the direction of the subject.
e) As an auxiliary verb preceded by the perfect converb describes the action as momentary.
f) The modal and perfect converbs of this verb preceded by the ablative case have the meaning of "beginning with, from, since."

23480.explain: -- yn erke; T. smon lam la dbang ba; S. pranidhāna- vaçitā. Mastery over one's (religious) aspira- tions which enable a Bo. to reveal himself in any of the cosmic fields to achieve enlightenment. jeke -- ; T. smon lam chen mo. Tne Great Prayer Meeting in Lhasa. uridu --; T. sngon gyi smon lam; S. pūrva- pranidhāna, Previous aspiration, vow made in a previous existence.

23481.explain: ITEGEKY ; T. skyabs su mchi ba; S. çaranam gam- To take refuge in. ITEGEL; T. mgon po; S. nātha. Lord, protector. S. refuge. See abural Applied to various deities. γurban xutuytan dur -- jabuyulxu; T. hphags pa gsum la skyabs su hgro ba or mchi ba; S. triçarana-gamana. The triple refuge in the γurban erdeni I take my refuge in the burxan, in the nom and in the xuvaray . This formula is a "declaration of intention" to become a Buddhist. It is also an indispensable part in the framework of a "liturgy" (bytygel yn ary-a, yal un sudur, xangyal, etc.). In later Bsm. it was enlarged by introducing a declaration to the effect that the faithful first takes his refuge in the several gurus (lamas), protectors of the faith, dakinis.

23483.explain: JAMA ; T. Gcin rje (Lord of death); S. Yama. God of death and hell. See Erlig and Pt.I. JEKE IZAΓUR tabun ; T. rigs Inga; S. panca-gotra or panca- kula. "Mystic " family or conclave as contrasted to the mythological families. The system which became important in "esoteric" Bsm.(Lamais) is an attempt of putting order into mythological chaos with regard to cosmology, macro- and micro- cosmos, soteriology, anatomy, in brief almost everything which could be subsumed under a pentad. They are: Masi geigylegci; T. Rnam par snang mdzad; S. Vairocana (center); Kødylesi ygei; T. Mi hkhrugs pa; S. Akshobhya (east); Erdeni γarxu jin orun; T. Rin chen hbyung gnas; S. Ratna-sam- bhava (south); Caylasi ygei gerelty; T. Hod dpag med; S. Amitābha (west); Byky tusa ji bytygegci; T. Dón yod grub pa; S. Amogha-siddhi (north). These Bus. are also called: "Buddhas of trans- cendent awareness" . See burxan. IZAΓURTAN y kybegyn; T. rigs kyi bu; S. kula-putra. A young man of good family; a clansman, gentle- mán. Frequent form of address in the sudur. IZAΓURTU; T. rigs can; S. kulika. Belonging to a mystic family. J JAMANDAG-A; S. Yamāntaka.Ep. of Erlig yn daisun. The most formidable among the doysit, blue, with 34 arms and 16 feet, eleven faces, the topmost being that of Manzusiri whose ferocious form he represents. JAMBAR byky josuyar; T. ji ltar, ji ltar bzhin du; S. katha. As, like, according to, commensurably with. mety; T. ji lta ba(r); S. yathā-bhūtam. As it really is, according to its ultimate being or "essence."

23489.explain: to another life; death. sansar un --; T. srid hpho ba; S. bhava-samkran- ti. Wandering through the circle of transmigrations.

23490.explain: T. Mthu chen thob; S. Mahā-sthāma-prāpta. He who has acquired great strength, one of the major Bos., often pendant to Nidyber yzegci .

23493.explain: JIDAM; T. yi dam; S. isht a - devatā; svādhi-daivatā , çraddhā-deva. A divinity chosen as personal pro- tector or patron by a lama, who selects him before initiation and never discloses his identity before his death. The lama feels himself under the personal surveillance and protection of his yidam during all his life. At his funeral procession a picture of the jidam is carried in front, facing the coffin. JIRTINCY ; T. hjig rten; S. loka ( dhātu ). The world. ED 464 a. ailaduyci; T. hjig rten mkhyen pa; S. lokavid. Knower of the world, ep. of the Bu. (a) traidhātuka dhātu, (b) tribhuvana, tribhavana. (a) Triple universe, the world of desire, forms, and formlessness. ED 256 b., (b) The three worlds: heaven, earth, and hades, the material, "revealed," and spiritual world.

23497.explain: KECEGYY jin tailburi; T. dkah hgrel; S panjikā. Com- mentary on difficult points of a text. KEI γurban mingyan --; T. stong gsum gyi khams; S. tri-sāhasra-loka-dhātu. The famous sudur jeke belge bilig baramid which exists in various versions, so called because it is considered as the Mother of all the Buddhas.

The Vehicle of the "Diamond" or "Thunderbolt, " that late ritualistic branch of Bsm. distinguishable by its excessive use of tarni, mandal, and empha- sis on ceremonies, and a legion of gods, demi- gods and spirits, and by a complicated soterio- logy and cosmology, integrating the macro-and micro cosmos. See Vacirdar-a. KøRYG bej-e; T. gzugs brnyan; S. pratibimba. Image of a deity; meditative image in the mind of a meditator. arban --; T. stobs bcu; S. daça-bala. The ten powers distinctive of a Bu. ED 262-263. one of the six baramid. KYLIL = mutur, which is more frequent ; T. phyag rgya ("seal", loan transl. from S. ); S. mudrā . Gesture, tie made with the hands in worship (cf. our folding the hands in prayer). See Pt.I under kylil and mutur.

23524.explain: the colloquial dynxor); S. kāla-cakra. The Wheel of Time. Name of a Tantric system, its personi- fication in a deity and its basic text, the Kālacakra sutra. Its teachings are an amalgamation of Hindu- ist and Buddhist elements. Claimed by its adherents to have been revealed by Šagjamuni himself as the mystery of mysteries it can be traced back to the 10th century AD. Its complex mandala showing all kinds of cosmic symbols referring to its doctrine is perhaps the most complicated assembly of symbols ever devised.

23535.explain: next Bu. to appear on earth, now supposed to be residing in Tysidyn orun as a bodisadu-a.

23536.explain: MAJ-A; T. sgyu ma; S. māyā . Illusion.

23537.explain: MANDAL; T. dkyil hkhor; S. mandala, A disk (as the sun disk); (in Tantrism) mystic wheels ( as of the four elements) located in the four centers of the body. See also Pt.I and Yhk. 128-138. un zang yile; T! dkyil hkhor gyi cho ga, dkyil chog; S. mandala-vidhi. Mandala ritual. yal -- ; T. sbyin sreg; S. homa. Fire or burnt offering. See Yhk. 150-16l. xoa -- . A plastic (usually metallic) mandala. See Yhk. I,16l and picture.

23538.explain: MANGΓALAM = ølzei xutuy ; T. bkra çis; S. mangala . Good fortune, happiness.

23539.explain: MANGLAI; T. mchog; S. agra. The very best, top.

23540.explain: MANI ; T ma ni; S. mani. Gem, jewelprecious stone; talisman; "mai, " is the name of the most fre- quently used invocation of the Lamaists: om mai padme hūm. See Pt.I.

23541.explain: MANTRA = tarni; T. sngags. Prayer, magic formula, sacred words. See Pt.I.

23542.explain: MANZUSIRI; T. Hjam dpal; S. ManjuçrI. One of the eight Great Bodhisattvas, hypostasis for the belge bilig,one of the three Jeke tørylkiten; his name is translated as Zøgelen coytu.

23543.explain: MARICI ; T. Hod zer can; S. Marici . Name of a goddess of light.

23544.explain: MASI ; T. rab (tu), cin tu. Represents the S. intensifiers ati-, vi-. pra-and'the word parama. -- ariluysan; T. rnam par day pa; S. vicuddhi. Complete purity. delgerenggyi; T. çin tu rgyas pa; S.(maha-) vaipulyà. Same as delgerenggyi. gegegen; T. rab gsal. Collection of minor rituals recited in regular daily services.

23545.explain: geigylyn zokijayci. T. Rnam par snang mdzad; S. Vairocana. One of the pentad of Bus. (izayurtu burxan); he presides over the upper most paradise. ketyrkei; T. rab hbyams pa; S prasara Eminent, distinguished, far-reaching, extending; scholar, learned person. narin toyusun = nab narin toyusun. -- sain. See xamuy sain. saitur; T. rab tu; represents S. su- and similar intensifying prefixes. saitur orusuluyci; T. rab tu gnas pa; S. supra - tishthita. Consecrated. suduluysan; T. cin tu sbyangs pa; S. praçrabdha = praçrabdhi. The cathartic (of body and mind); ED 388 a: praçrabdha, pracrabdhi ("allayed, stilled; alleviation; calmed"). tonilxu; T. rnam par grol ba; S. vimukti, vimoksha. Emancipation, deliverance: ED 497 a.

23546.explain: MASIDA tein byged ilyaxui; T. rab tu rnam par hbyed pa; S. pravicaya Transcendental analysis, having noumenon as its object; see tein byged ilyaxui. One of the two fundamental forms of higher vision (vi- paçyana. See ylemzi yzekyi). MAXA (fr. S.) See also maha-a. (Double "a" [ two teeth in M. transliteration of S. words] represent long ā).

23547.explain: MAXABUD (fr.S.) dørben; T. hbyung ba chen po bzhi; S. catvāri mahā-bhūtāni. The four "great" elements which do not derive from anything and are the transcendental bases of certain qualities of things : earth (sirui), hard; water (usun), flexible; fire (yal), hot; air (salkin) yielding. See next entry. -- ece boluysan; T. hbyung ba las gyur pa; S. bhautika. Originated from the maxabud: material belonging to the sphere of perceptions by the senses. ED 412-3.

23548.explain: Great king, emperor. See maxa. dørben --. The Four Great Kings = xayan, jeke = jirtynci ji tedkygci.

23549.explain: MAXASUNG; T. sems dpah chen po; S. mahāsattva. A Great Being, ep. of Bos. ED 426 b.

23550.explain: MEDEGDEGYN ; T. es bya; S. jneya. The knowable.

23551.explain: MEDEKYI; T. (rnam par) es pa; S. vijnāna. States of consciousness, last of the five coyca. They are classified according to the senses: conscious- ness of vision (nidyn), audition ( cikin), olfaction (xabar), gustation (kelen), touch ( bej-e).

23552.explain: MINYKEI kemen barimtalaxu; T. bdag gis hdzin pa; S. mamakāra. Egoism, selfishness.

23556.explain: dyr barimtalaxu; T. dngos dzin; S. mamakāra. The idea that something belongs to me, is mine. MØN cinar (a); T. ngo bo nyid, rang bzhin nyid; S. svabhāva. ED 6l5 b. Intrinsic nature, self- nature. (b) T. de bzhin nyid; S. tathatā, tathatva. suchness, thatness, ultimate reality as contrasted to phenomenal appearance . ED 248. (c) T. de kho na nyid; S. tattva. Ultimate re- ality. See nom un cinar, belge cinar. cinar (inu) xoyusun; T. rang bzhin stong pa; S. svabhāva-çūnya. Intrinsically or essentially void, without substance, (merely) relational. sedkilyn -- cinar;Tsems kyi rang bzhin; S. citta-sva bhāva. Proper or true nature of the mind. tegsí saca -- cinar; T. rang bzhin mnyam pa nyid; S. svabhāva-samatā. Equal by its ( their) very nature. MøN cinartu; T. bdag nyid can; S. atmaka. Having for its substance or essence, being a personi- fication of ... MøNGKE busu; T. mi rtag pa; S. anitya. Transitory. busu jin cinar; T. mi rag pa nyid; S. anityatā. Transitoriness (of all phenomena ). orun; T. rang bzhin gnas. Eternity, the indestruct- ible element, the absolute nirvana. ygei; T. rtag (pa) med (pa); S. anitya(tā ). With- out eternity, transitoriness. MØR ; T. lam; S. pratipad, patha, mārga. Path or road, esp. the path ofthe holy truths. yn zerge; T. lam gyi rim pa, lam rim; S. patha- krama. Sequence, steps on the way towards buddha- hood, title of various works, of which the Lam rim chen mo by Tsong kha pa has become the most famous. bisilyaxui jin --; T. bsgom pahi lam; S. bhāvanā- mārga. Via contemplativa. tyridkyi jin --; T. hgog pahi lam; S. nirodha marga. The path of suppression (of suffering). See tyridkyi (and) yneker. xutuytan u naiman gesigyn y --; T. hphags pahi lam yan lag brgyad pa; S. āryāshtāngga-mārga. Theeightfold path of the holy ones proclaimed by the Bu. in his first sermon. Its members are: yneker yzel, T. yang dag pahi Ita ba, S. samyag drshti, "right" or "correct views"; yneker onul, T. yang dag pahi rtogs pa, S. samyag-samkalpa, "right understanding or thinking"; yneker kelen, T. yang dag pahi ngag, S.samyag vāk, "right speech"; yneker yiles yn ecys, T. yang dag páhi las kyi mthah, S, samyak-karmānta, "right aims" ; yneker ami- dural, T. yang dag pahi htsho ba, S. samyag-

23557.explain: ājiva, "right life; yneker simdan, T. yang dag pahi rtsol bà, S. samyag vyāyāma,"right effort"; yneker duradxui, T. yang dag pahi dran pa, S. samyak-smrti, 'right mindfulness"; yneker samadi, T. yang dag pahi ting nge hdzin, S. samyak-samādhi,"right me- ditative concentration." yly surxui --; T. mi slob pahi lam; S. açaiksha-mārga. The path of one who needs no longer training, as a daisun i daruyci. yzekyi jin --; T. mthong bahi lam; s. darçana-mārga. The intuitive path. MØRGYKY(I) ; T. phyag tshal ba; S. abhivandana,namaskr-. To salute. See Pt.I. Salutation of the deity is the first ritual act when entering the temple; it is also an important symbol when conducting a bytygel ary-a.

23558.explain: ājiva, "right life; yneker simdan, T. yang dag pahi rtsol bà, S. samyag vyāyāma,"right effort"; yneker duradxui, T. yang dag pahi dran pa, S. samyak-smrti, 'right mindfulness"; yneker samadi, T. yang dag pahi ting nge hdzin, S. samyak-samādhi,"right me- ditative concentration." yly surxui --; T. mi slob pahi lam; S. açaiksha-mārga. The path of one who needs no longer training, as a daisun i daruyci. yzekyi jin --; T. mthong bahi lam; s. darçana-mārga. The intuitive path. MØRGYKY(I) ; T. phyag tshal ba; S. abhivandana,namaskr-. To salute. See Pt.I. Salutation of the deity is the first ritual act when entering the temple; it is also an important symbol when conducting a bytygel ary-a.

23559.explain: NAB narin toyusun = masi narin; T. rdul phra rab; S. paramānu. Finest dust, smallest particle ima- ginable, "atom."

23561.explain: NAIDANGΓUI; T. phrag dog; S. irshā, İrshya. Envy jealousy.

23562.explain: NAIRAΓ; T. dpe byad; S. anuvyanjana. The (80) minor distinguishing marks of the body of the Bu.

23563.explain: unal --; T. ltung ba bçags pa; S. pāpa- deçanã. Confession of sins.

23564.explain: NAMZAR ; T. snam sbyar; S. samghātī. Garment pieced together of small strips, one of the three garments of the Buddhist priests.

23565.explain: NARIN tailburi; T. dkah hgrel; S. panjikā. Commentary on the difficult points of a work.

23566.explain: NASUN u erketen; T. tshe la dbang ba; S. ayur-vaçitā. Mastery over one's life, i. e. freedom to stay in the sansar as long as desired; third mastery of a Bo. -- a tegylter, -- luya tegylter = amin xabijatu; T. tshe dang ldan pa; S. ayusmat. Long-living, a form of address with venerable disciples. ED 102. jegydkeky; T. tshe hpho ba; S. cyuti. Transfer of life; to die and be reborn. -- u yxayan; T. tshehi rig byed; S. ayurveda. The science of longevit. medicine.

23567.explain: NENG Very, transl. S. prefix ati-. ketyregsen; T. thal ches par gyur; S. atiprasanga. An overstatement, exaggeration.

23568.explain: NER-E øngge; T. ming dang gzugs; S. nāma-rūpa. Name and form, the fourth link in the twelve-fold concatenation

23576.explain: MøRGYL un silyg; T. phyag tshal gyi tshigs bcad. Hymn of salutation or praise. MUNGXAΓ ;T. ma rig pa; S. avidyã. Non-wisdom, non-knowledge (not ignorance); it is the first link in the chain of correlations (sityn barilduly-a). The M. word is a semantic substitute. MUNI ( fr. S) T. thub pa; S. muni. Hermit, saint,sage. MUTUR ; T. phyag rgya; S. mudrā. See Pt. I under mutur and kylil. -- un abuly-a; T. phyag len. Procedure, agenda. N called sityn barilduly-a. Note that the second part of the binom sees to reflect the Chinese translation of the S., namely øngge "color" and Ch. se "color" represent here S. rūpa, T. gzugs, "form". NEREIDKEL ; T. tha snyad; S. vyavahāra. Conventional concept or term. ED 516 b. NIDYBER yzegci; T. pyan ras gzigs; S. Avalokiteçvara. "Looking with his eyes" - name of the most famous of all the Bos. He is popularly referred to as Arijabalo.The name is explained as meaning ziryuyan zyil amitan nuyud i nidyber yzegci; T. hgro drug sems can rnams la spyan ras gzigs, "eyeing the six kinds of amitan" (compassionately). yzegci erketen; T. Spyan ras gzig dbang phyug; S. Avalokitecvara. The complete name of Nidyber yzegci, nidyber translating Avalokita = spyan ras gzigs and erketen dbang phyugs S. ivara. NIDYN; T. mig; S. cakshus. Eye as the internal base of vision. See tøryn tygekyi. -- y erketen; T. mig gi dbang po; S, cakshus. The faculty of vision, "organ" of vision. -- y tein medekyi; T. mig gi rnam par çes pa; S. cakshur-vijnana. Visual consciousness, i. e. becoming conscious of seeing something . belge bilig yn -- tegysygsen; T. ye es kyi spyan dang ldan pa; S. jnāna-cakshus. Possessing the eye of wisdom. NIΓUCA ji bariyci; T. gsang ba hdzin pa; S. guhya- dhara. Holder of mysteries, ep. of the Bo. Vacirbani. jin blama; T. gsang bahi bla ma; S. guhya - guru. Guide in mysteries, mystagogue. jin ezen; T. Gsang bdag; S. Guhya-pati. Lord of Mysteries, ep. of Vacirbani.

23580.explain: orun a masida oruysan; T. gsang bahi gnas la cin tu gzhugs pa; S. guhyānupravishta. Having deeply penetrated into the mysteries.

23581.explain: NIGENTE xarin -iregci; T. lan cig phyir hong; S. sakrd- agāmin. One who only once returns, i.e. becomes only once more reincarnated. NIGYL ; T. sdig pa mi dge ba; S. pāpa, açubha. Sin, trans- gression. -- i daruyci; T. sdig hjoms; S. aghahantr. Sin- destroyer, ep. of the Bu. yn yge; T. mi dgehi gtam; S. akuçala-kathā. Un- virtuous accounts or stories ( which the monk should avoid). NIGYLESKYI; T.snying rje; S. karunā . Compassion, 2nd of the four boundless states. See caylasi ygei. jeke; T. thugs rje chen po; S. mahākārunika. (He) of great compassion, ep. of Nidyber yzegci. NILXA; T. byis pa; S. bala. "Child", fool (figuratively in regard to understanding Bsm. ).

23582.explain: NIRVAN ; T. zhi ba; S. nirvāna. Nirvana; calm. i ecylgegci; T. zhi mthar byed. Destroyer of nirva- na's calm; the lord of tle simuns. i eregci; T. zhi ba tshol ba. Seeking the (quiescent) nirvana, as the bradikabud. orusil ygei -- ; T. mi gnas pahi mya ngan las hdas pa; S. apratishthita-nirvāna. The nirvana which is not permanently fixed, a nirvana in which the tegyn- cilen irègsen returns to worldly life to save amitan. ED 48 a. ylegsen coyca ygei -- ; T. phung po lhag pa med pahi mya ngan las hdas pa; S. nir-upadhiçesha-nirvāa. Nirvana without a remainder (of the five coyca). Note: nirupadhiesha, not upadhiçesha. upadhi = skandha, M. coyca. See ED 300 a. Contrasted with next term. -- ylegsen coycatu bari nirvan; T. phung po lhag ma dang bcas pahi mya ngan las hdas pa; S. sopādhiçesa- nirvāna (i.e. with the five coyca somehow preserved).

23583.explain: NISVANIS; T. nyon mongs; S. kleça.(The defilement or corruption through) passions. ED 198 a. baraysan ; T. zag pa zad pa; S. kshīāç rava, kshināsrava. One whose nisvanis are already exhausted or eliminated (first of the erdem of a siravay). ygei; T. nyon mongs med pa; S. nishkleça . Without defilement or corruption. izayur un --; T. rtsa bahi nyon mongs; S. mūla-kleça. Original defilements: delusion, hatred, and lust acc. to Asanga. NOM; T. chos; S. dharma (Buddhist) religion, transl. as LAW, norm, etc. NOM baiyulxu; T. chos btsugs pa. To found, introduce the (Buddh.) religion. See also nom ud. busu; T. chos min; S. adharma. Irreligion. dur batu boluysan; T. chos la brtan pa; S. dharma-drdha. Firmly grounded in religion. dur erke; T. chos la dbang ba; S. dharma-vaçitā. Mastery over the (preaching of) Bsm. due to elo- quence and knowledge, seventh mastery of the Bo. ece γaruysan; T. chos las hbyung ba; S. dharmato nigata. Coming out of or from the Buddhist religion, springing from the nom ud, q. v. i edleky; T. chos la spyod pa; S. dharma-caryā. To perform one's religious duties, practice re- ligion; one of the ten activities performed with reference to the doctrine, such as copying a sacred text, worshiping, alms giving, etc. ED 278 a. luy-a tegysygsen; T. chos ldan; S. dhārmika. Righteous, just. nomlaxu; T. chos hchad pa; S. dharma - deçanā. Preaching of the Bu. religion. un ayar; T. chos (kyi) dbyings; S. dharma-dhātu. The realm of religion; the realm or sphere of the nom ud. ED 278-279. un axu josun; T. chos kyi gnas lugs. The natural state of the nom ud, q.v. un belge cinar; T. chos rnams kyi mtshan nyid; S. dharma-lakshana. The nom ud as momentary manifestations. un bej-e; T. chos (kyi) sku; S. dharmakāya. The "absolute" body of a Buddha, the absolute perso- nified or imagined as a Bu. ED 277 a-b. See bej-e.  un boyda; T. chos (kyl) rje; S. dharma-svāmin. A higher clerical title, also exorcist. -- un cinar; T. chos nyid; S. dharmatā .True nature, reality, the whole of the whole = dharma- kaya, the essence of the essences. ED 278 a-b. un cinar un møn cinar; T. chos nyid kyi ngo ba; S. dharma(tā)-svabhāva. The latent nom ud, nom ud as potentials. See nom ud. -- un debel. Monk's or lama's official dress, ca- nonicals; cloth wrappings for religious scriptures. -- un erkety; T. chos kyi dbang phyug; S. dharme- vara. Lord of the Buddhist religion, the Bu. un jabudal; T. chos spyod; S. dharmacaryā Religious act; religious conduct. ED 278 a. -- un josun; T. chos lugs. Religion, religious sect or school; religious ceremony or rite. -- un kyrdyn i orciyulxui; T. chos kyi hkhor lo skor ba; S. dharma-cakra-pravartana. The turn- ing of the wheel of religion = preaching of the Buddhist religion. ED 277 a. un kyrdyn; T. chos kyi hkhor lo; S. dharma-cakra. The wheel of the (Buddh.)religion, symbol of Bsm.

23585.explain: un øglyge; T. chos sbyin; S. dharma-dāna. Gift of the doctrine, the greatest of all gifts. un sakiyulsun; T. chos skyong; S. dharma-pāla. Protector(s) of the Religion, refers esp. to various group of deities, mostly of terrible aspect, charged with annihilating all enemies of the faith, incltding humans and demons and deities of heretic creeds. un xayan; T. chos kyi rgyal po; S. dharma-rāja. King of Religion, title of deities, esp. of Erlig (Yama), who metes out justice in the after-life; also a high ecclesiastical title, which is sometimes given to laic high-ranking benefactors of the Church. un xauli; T. chos srol. Religious custom(s), rite(s), ceremonies. un zang yile; T. chos kyi cho ga; S. dharma-vidhi. Religious rite. ygei. Same as nom busu. xolical ygei --, ese xolicalduxu --; T. ma hdres pahi chos; S. avenika-dharma. A series of qualities exclusively belonging to a Bu. or Bo. ED 108-9. xuricaxui --; T. hkhrig pahi chos; S. grāma-dharma. Unchastity. NOM ud (plural of nom). The word nom (S.dharma) acquired a very special meaning as a philosophical term by designating the irreducible elements for the construction of a pluralistic world conception com- prising both external and internal phenomena. There are various attempts at rendering this term in English. such as "element, ""essence", "mental dates", "mentals", none of them is quite satisfactory.Datum pl. data, might perhaps be acceptable, if one ignores the fact that a datum, by its very etymology, presupposes a subject. On account of this difficulty the M. term nom ud has been retained in this word list. NOMTU; T. chos ldan; S. dharmin; dharmika. Religious, just; pious, righteous. debel; T. bla gos; S. cīvara. Monk's robe, canonicals worn at religious services.

23587.explain: OITARIUI; T. bar snang; S. antariksha. Space, spatial ether, heaven, the space where the evoked deity appears. ber jabuyci: T nkhah hgro; S. dāka. The male counterpart of a k ini. jin orun; T. nam khahi khams; S. ākāça-dhātū. Spatial ether (not ir uded in the four elements). emyneki --; T. mdun gyi nam mkhah; S. antariksha. OFUTATA NOMUTADXAL ; T. hdul ba; S. vin aya. Monk's dis- cipline and the section of the Scriptures which deals with it. NOMUTADXAΓDAXU ; T. gdul bar bya; S. vineya. Some- body to be conyerted to the Buddh. religion. NOMUΓADXAXUI bariyci; T. hdul ba hdzin pa; S. vinaya- dhara. Retaining (in memory) the Vinai code, an ecclesiastic title.

23592.explain: NØKYR, NøKYD. Retainer, group or conclave of gods, demigods, etc. evoked as associates of the chief deity, their lord (ezen), in the bytygel yn ary-a. șadun; T. bçes gnyen; S. kalyāna-mitra. Spiritual friend or guide.: ED 174 a.

23594.explain: NUTA bayuyaxu; T. gtan la dbab pa; S. nirnaya(na). Complete ascertaiment, settling or deciding. NUTADA sanaxui; T. bsam gtan; S. dhyāna. Meditation, the procedure of samadi. NUTALAL; T. gtan tshigs; S. hetu. Affirmation, syllo- gism, conclusion, logic, reason. - un uxayan; T. gtan tshigs (kyi) rig pa; S. hetuvidyā . The science of logic, dialectics.

23595.explain: NUTALALCI; T. gtan tshigs mkhan; S. hetuka. Logi- cian. dialectician.

23597.explain: The part of the sky in front of the bytygelcin where he expects the evoked deities to appear.

23598.explain: OIUΓATA; T. yongs su; S. pari-. Completely, perfectly. adxaxu; T. yongs su rtogs pa; S. pari-kalpa. Imagination, figment. ED 320 b. ariγun; T. yongs su dag pa; S. pari-çuddha. Wholly clean or pure; holy. arilyaxu; T. yongs su sbyong ba; S. pari-çodhana. Complete purification . ED 330 b (paricodhaka).

23599.explain: nye bar. The M. and T. adverbs substitute for the S. pref. upa-. sedkil i -- ayulxu; T. nye bar bzhag pa, nyer bzhag; S. upasthāna. Application (of one's mind). See duradxui.

23600.explain: masi xurca --; T. dbang po in tu rno ba; S. tikshnendriya. A keen sense organ; an extra-sensitive sense.

23601.explain: sonusuysan; T. mang po thos pa; S. bahuçruta. Of much hearing, i.e. learning. One of the erdem of the sivarag and of the nøkyr sadun. ED 399 b.

23602.explain: phal po che; S. avatamsaka. A large number. -- burxan; T. sangs rgyas phal po che; S. Buddha-avatam- saka. A "collection of Buddhas", also a group of Scriptures. ED 7la.

23603.explain: hthob pa; S. prāpti. "Reach', the force which regulates the cooperation of the nom ud ("data") at any given gsan (moment in the con- tinuum). See nom ud. ygei; T. hthob pa med pa; S. a-prapti. The force which excludes incompatible nom ud from appear- ing at a given moment. ( usually nazalized "o"). This mystic syllbable is

23605.explain: rtog pa; S. kalpa. (False) thought. ED l72 b yneker -- : Right thought. See mør.

23606.explain: sa, Place. γarxui jin --; T.hbung gnas; S. ākara. (Place of) origin, source.

23607.explain: khams; S. dhātu. Plane of existence. amitan u --; T.sems can gyi khams; S. sattva- dhātu. The plane of existence of the amitan. birid yn --; T. yi dvags kyi khams; S. preta-vishaya. The sphere of the starveling ghosts. yurban --; T. khams gsum; S. traidhatuka. The triple universe, namely the kyseky orun, øngge jin orun, øngge ygei jin orun.

23608.explain: yu; S. vishaya. Sphere, range, scope. See višai. nidyn y -- . The range of the eye or vision.

23609.explain: zhing ; S. kshetra. The "field" of a Buddha, his (mystical) country over which he,surrounded by by his nøkyd, is the spiritual ruler.

23610.explain: gzhi; S.ālaya. Base. See ED l06 under ālaya-vijnāna.

23611.explain: gnas; S. sthāna. Scientific discipline. uxayan u --; T. rig (pahi) gnas; S. vidyā-sthāna. Science, usuallyfive branches; grammar, logic, metaphysics, medicine, and craftsmanshift (art).

23612.explain: sa; S. bhūmi. Any or all of the stages in the spiritual developme nt; ED 4ll a. bodisaduv-a jin -- ; T. byang chub sems dpahi sa; S. bodhisattva-bhumi.
